children.title: Attention Is All You Need
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/Attention Is All You Need
children.summary: The section titled 'Attention Is All You Need' lists the authors of the paper, their affiliations (primarily Google Brain and Google Research), and their contact information. It also includes a footnote detailing the equal contributions of the authors to the work.

children.title: Abstract
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/Abstract
children.summary: The abstract introduces the Transformer, a new network architecture based solely on attention mechanisms that dispenses with recurrence and convolutions. It highlights that this model is superior in quality, more parallelizable, and requires significantly less training time compared to dominant sequence transduction models. The text details performance results on machine translation tasks (WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French), noting state-of-the-art BLEU scores achieved with reduced training costs. Additionally, it mentions successful application of the Transformer to English constituency parsing.

children.title: 1 Introduction
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/1 Introduction
children.summary: The section introduces recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and their limitations regarding sequential computation and parallelization. It discusses attention mechanisms as a solution for modeling dependencies but notes they are often used with RNNs. The authors propose the Transformer, a model architecture that eschews recurrence entirely in favor of an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output, allowing for significant parallelization.

children.title: 2 Background
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/2 Background
children.summary: The section discusses the background of sequence modeling, focusing on reducing sequential computation. It reviews models like Extended Neural GPU, ByteNet, and ConvS2S that use convolutional neural networks. It also covers self-attention (intra-attention) mechanisms used in tasks like reading comprehension and summarization, as well as end-to-end memory networks. The text concludes by stating that the Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention without using sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution.

children.title: 3 Model Architecture
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/3 Model Architecture
children.summary: The section titled '3 Model Architecture' introduces the standard encoder-decoder structure used in competitive neural sequence transduction models. It describes how an encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations to a sequence of continuous representations, and how a decoder subsequently generates an output sequence one element at a time in an auto-regressive manner.

children.title: 3.1 Encoder and Decoder Stacks
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/3 Model Architecture/3.1 Encoder and Decoder Stacks
children.summary: Section 3.1 describes the architecture of the Encoder and Decoder stacks in the Transformer model. The encoder consists of a stack of N=6 identical layers, each containing two sub-layers: a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise fully connected feed-forward network. Both are surrounded by residual connections followed by layer normalization. The decoder also uses a stack of N=6 identical layers but includes an additional third sub-layer that performs multi-head attention over the encoder's output. This sub-layer is masked to prevent attending to subsequent positions, ensuring predictions depend only on known outputs.

children.title: 3.2 Attention
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/3 Model Architecture/3.2 Attention
children.summary: Section 3.2 introduces the concept of an attention function, defining it as a mapping from a query and a set of key-value pairs to an output vector. It states that the query, keys, values, and output are all vectors, and the output is computed as a weighted sum.

children.title: 3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/3 Model Architecture/3.2 Attention/3.2.1 Scaled Dot-Product Attention
children.summary: This section defines Scaled Dot-Product Attention, an attention mechanism where weights are computed by taking the dot product of queries and keys, scaling them by the square root of the key dimension ($\sqrt{d_k}$), and applying a softmax function. It presents the matrix formulation for computing outputs from packed query, key, and value matrices. The text compares this method to additive attention, noting that while theoretically similar, dot-product attention is faster and more space-efficient due to optimized matrix multiplication code. It also explains that scaling is necessary to prevent dot products from growing too large in magnitude for high-dimensional vectors, which would push the softmax into regions with extremely small gradients.

children.title: 3.2.2 Multi-Head Attention
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/3 Model Architecture/3.2 Attention/3.2.2 Multi-Head Attention
children.summary: Section 3.2.2 introduces Multi-Head Attention, a mechanism that improves upon single attention functions by linearly projecting queries, keys, and values into multiple lower-dimensional spaces (h times). These projections are then processed in parallel using the attention function, allowing the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces.

children.title: 3.2.3 Applications of Attention in our Model
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/3 Model Architecture/3.2 Attention/3.2.3 Applications of Attention in our Model
children.summary: Section 3.2.3 describes the three ways multi-head attention is applied in the Transformer model: encoder-decoder attention (where queries come from the decoder and keys/values from the encoder), self-attention in the encoder (all keys, values, and queries originate from the previous encoder layer), and masked self-attention in the decoder (which prevents leftward information flow to preserve auto-regressive properties by masking illegal connections).

children.title: 3.3 Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/3 Model Architecture/3.3 Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks
children.summary: Section 3.3 describes the Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks used in the model's encoder and decoder layers. These are fully connected networks applied independently to each position, consisting of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation function in between. The text provides the mathematical formula for this operation (FFN) and specifies the dimensionalities: input/output dimension ($d_{model}$) is 512, and the inner-layer dimensionality ($d_{ff}$) is 2048.

children.title: 3.4 Embeddings and Softmax
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/3 Model Architecture/3.4 Embeddings and Softmax
children.summary: Section 3.4 describes the use of learned embeddings to convert input and output tokens into vectors of dimension d_model. It also details the application of a linear transformation and softmax function to predict next-token probabilities, noting that the weight matrix is shared between the embedding layers and the pre-softmax transformation.

children.title: 3.5 Positional Encoding
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/3 Model Architecture/3.5 Positional Encoding
children.summary: Section 3.5 discusses the necessity of positional encoding in models without recurrence or convolution to capture sequence order. It details the use of sine and cosine functions with different frequencies as the chosen method, providing the specific mathematical formulas for these encodings. The text explains that wavelengths form a geometric progression and justifies this choice by its ability to allow the model to learn relative positions via linear functions. It also notes an experiment comparing this sinusoidal approach to learned embeddings, finding them nearly identical but preferring the sinusoidal version for better extrapolation capabilities.

children.title: 4 Why Self-Attention
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/4 Why Self-Attention
children.summary: This section compares self-attention layers with recurrent and convolutional layers based on three criteria: computational complexity per layer, the amount of parallelizable computation (measured by sequential operations), and path length for long-range dependencies. It references Table 1 to highlight that self-attention connects all positions with a constant number of sequential operations, making it faster than recurrent layers in terms of complexity when sequence lengths are large.

children.title: 5 Training
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/5 Training

children.title: 5.1 Training Data and Batching
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/5 Training/5.1 Training Data and Batching
children.summary: This section describes the training data and batching strategy. It details the use of the WMT 2014 English-German dataset (approx. 4.5 million pairs) and the larger WMT 2014 English-French dataset (36M sentences). Sentences were encoded using byte-pair encoding with vocabularies of about 37,000 and 32,000 tokens respectively. Batching was performed by approximate sequence length, with each batch containing approximately 25,000 source and target tokens.

children.title: 5.2 Hardware and Schedule
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/5 Training/5.2 Hardware and Schedule
children.summary: Section 5.2 describes the hardware and training schedule used for the models. It specifies that training was performed on a machine equipped with 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs. The section details the step time (0.4 seconds) and total duration (100,000 steps or 12 hours) for base models, as well as the step time (1.0 second) and duration (300,000 steps or 3.5 days) for big models.

children.title: 5.3 Optimizer
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/5 Training/5.3 Optimizer
children.summary: Section 5.3 describes the optimizer used for training, which is the Adam optimizer with specific parameters (β1=0.9, β2=0.98, ε=10^-9). It details a learning rate schedule that linearly increases for the first 4000 warmup steps and then decreases proportionally to the inverse square root of the step number.

children.title: 5.4 Regularization
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/5 Training/5.4 Regularization
children.summary: Section 5.4 introduces the regularization techniques employed during training, stating that three types are used.

children.title: Residual Dropout
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/5 Training/5.4 Regularization/Residual Dropout
children.summary: The section describes the application of dropout in the Transformer model. It specifies that dropout is applied to the output of each sub-layer before it is added to the input and normalized, as well as to the sums of embeddings and positional encodings in both encoder and decoder stacks. For the base model, a dropout rate (P_drop) of 0.1 is used.

children.title: Label Smoothing
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/5 Training/5.4 Regularization/Label Smoothing
children.summary: The section describes the use of label smoothing during training with a value of epsilon_ls = 0.1, citing reference [36]. It notes that while this technique hurts perplexity by making the model more unsure, it improves accuracy and BLEU score.

children.title: 6 Results
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/6 Results

children.title: 6.1 Machine Translation
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/6 Results/6.1 Machine Translation
children.summary: Section 6.1 discusses the results of the Transformer model on WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation tasks. It highlights that the big Transformer model achieved state-of-the-art BLEU scores (28.4 for EN-DE, 41.0 for EN-FR) at a fraction of the training cost compared to previous models. The section details the experimental setup, including the use of 8 P100 GPUs, averaging checkpoints for base and big models, beam search parameters, and early stopping strategies.

children.title: 6.2 Model Variations
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/6 Results/6.2 Model Variations
children.summary: Section 6.2 introduces an ablation study designed to evaluate the importance of different components within the Transformer architecture. The text explains that the authors varied their base model in different ways and measured the resulting changes in performance specifically on the English-to-German translation task.

children.title: 6.3 English Constituency Parsing
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/6 Results/6.3 English Constituency Parsing
children.summary: The page presents Table 3, which details variations on the Transformer architecture and their performance metrics (PPL, BLEU, parameters) on the English-to-German translation development set (newstest2013). The table compares a base model against several ablation studies labeled (A) through (E), varying parameters like attention heads, dimensions, dropout, and positional embeddings. Below the table, the text discusses these results, noting that reducing key size hurts quality and that bigger models perform better. Section 6.3 introduces experiments on English Constituency Parsing using the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) portion of the Penn Treebank.

children.title: 7 Conclusion
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/7 Conclusion
children.summary: The section summarizes the paper's contribution of the Transformer, a sequence transduction model based entirely on attention that replaces recurrent layers with multi-headed self-attention. It highlights that the model achieves new state-of-the-art results on WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation tasks and outperforms previous ensembles. The authors also outline future plans to extend the model to other modalities like images and audio.

children.title: Acknowledgements
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/Acknowledgements
children.summary: The section expresses gratitude to Nal Kalchbrenner and Stephan Gouws for their comments, corrections, and inspiration.

children.title: References
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/References
children.summary: This page contains the conclusion of a research paper on the Transformer model, specifically its application to English constituency parsing. It features Table 4, which compares the performance (WSJ 23 F1 scores) of the Transformer against various other parsers under different training settings (discriminative, semi-supervised, multi-task). The text discusses the results, highlighting that the Transformer outperforms previous models despite lacking task-specific tuning. The page also includes an acknowledgements section and the beginning of the references list.

children.title: Attention Visualizations
children.path: Attention Is All You Need.pdf/Root/Attention Visualizations
children.summary: This section, titled 'Attention Visualizations', presents three figures (3, 4, and 5) that illustrate the behavior of attention mechanisms in a neural network model. Figure 3 shows an example of an attention head following long-distance dependencies to complete a phrase. Figure 4 demonstrates two attention heads involved in anaphora resolution, showing how they link pronouns like 'its' to their antecedents. Figure 5 provides examples of attention heads learning to perform tasks related to sentence structure.
